claim: Cases of ARFID are also on the rise, increasing by 305 percent from 2018 to 2022, according to a 2023 FAIR Health white paper.
label: PARTIALLY_TRUE
annotatorNote: [AI label: Claude, 2026-10-13 - not yet checked by the human annotator] FAIR Health, 'Spotlight on Eating Disorders: An Analysis of Private Healthcare Claims' (release 16 Nov 2023; AJMC 15 Nov 2023): from 2018 to 2022 eating-disorder claim lines rose as a percentage of all medical claim lines, 'avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) by 305 percent'. Figure, years and source hold; what rose is ARFID's share of insurance claim lines, not cases, and FAIR Health notes ARFID's diagnosis code only dates from 2017, so it rose from a low base. PARTIALLY_TRUE for calling claim lines 'cases'; TRUE if read loosely.
